A Ruby you can embed,
written in Go.

go-embedded-ruby (rbgo) is a from-scratch Ruby — lexer, parser, compiler, bytecode VM and an AOT backend — that embeds in any Go program and cross-compiles to a single CGO-free binary. Built in the open as a digital common (commun numérique), free to use, study, modify and share under the BSD-3-Clause licence.

Why rbgo

Everything a Ruby runtime gives you — as a Go library.

No FFI, no libruby, no system Ruby. Drop a genuine, monkey-patchable Ruby object model into your Go binary and ship it anywhere.

🧩

Embeddable

A real object model — classes, mixins, method_missing, metaprogramming, Fiber. The Go API is deliberately small today: ruby.Run(src, out) runs a program on a fresh VM and writes its output to one writer. Calling a Ruby method from Go is not exposed yet.

📦

One static binary

CGO=0 by default. Tested on amd64, arm64, riscv64, loong64, ppc64le, s390x, 386 and arm; compiles for every GOOS/GOARCH Go supports — 47 targets, the BSDs, AIX, Solaris, mips and Plan 9 included (Plan 9 is vetted, not run).

⚡

AOT for integer kernels

Ahead-of-time compilation of integer-bound methods to unboxed Go. Measured on this project’s own micro-benchmarks (darwin/arm64, whole-process wall time): 8.7× MRI+YJIT on the tight-loop case, 2.0× on recursive fib(35). Only methods the compiler can lower benefit.

✅

Conformance, measured

23,672 ruby/spec language/ + core/ examples pass, gated in CI file by file: no spec file may pass fewer examples than its recorded row, so a regression is named rather than absorbed in a total. Only language/ and core/ are swept: library/, optional/, command_line/ and security/ are not run, so this is not a percentage of Ruby. Those guards now resolve at Ruby 4.0.9 — the version this runtime reports, and the latest MRI release — so the examples behind a ruby_version_is "4.0" guard are counted, and those behind ruby_version_is ""..."4.0" are no longer asked for. The move was measured before it was made, both engines built from one commit minus the version string: +144 passing, and 27 examples that went red — a figure no pass total shows, found by comparing the two runs' failure descriptions. Front-end: ~100% of valid Ruby parsed across Rails + Puppet (2026-06).

🔒

Closed-world builds

rbgo build --closed bakes the program to bytecode and drops the front-end for a smaller binary.

🌿
